issues.description: extract_arch_from_url can silently return None, producing a garbage URL
issues.detail: If the regex doesn't match, arch is None and the f-string happily builds '.../latest/None/Packages/...'. The patch then appends that nonsense to the URL list and nothing complains until a build later fails to fetch it. Either raise on no-match or have the caller refuse to construct a URL. Don't swallow the failure.

issues.description: nevra[0] indexes the first character of the filename, not the first letter of the package name
issues.detail: Koji's canonical path is .../Packages/<first-letter-of-name>/<nevra>. nevra here is the full filename like 'glibc-2.39-1.fc40.x86_64.rpm', so nevra[0].lower() happens to work for 'glibc' but breaks the moment the URL has any prefix, leading dot, or unexpected component. Parse the package name properly, don't pun on string[0].

issues.description: Hardcoded koji base URL and arch list with no constant, no config, no test
issues.detail: kojipkgs.fedoraproject.org/repos-dist/coreos-pool and the four-arch list are baked into a helper with no module-level constant and no unit test. When koji moves the path or a new arch lands (riscv64 is coming), someone has to re-discover this function. Lift the constants, add one test that exercises a fedora-updates URL through the transform.

issues.description: Race condition between bump-lockfile merge and koji tag is documented but not mitigated
issues.detail: The commit message acknowledges that the crafted URL may not exist yet because coreos-koji-tagger runs after merge. That's a real failure mode for hermetic builds and there's no retry, no verification, no warning in the tool itself. At minimum log which URLs were synthesized so a failed Konflux build is debuggable without reading this commit.

issues.description: Dead-code path: prioritization logic in query_packages_location is now pointless
issues.detail: You removed the comment explaining the dnf5 workaround but left the 'if coreos-pool in url or not existing_url' prioritization in place, even though every URL gets rewritten downstream by use_koji_url_only. Either drop the prioritization (the rewrite makes it moot) or document why both layers exist. Two mechanisms doing the same job is how bugs hide.

issues.description: 'koji_url_base in url' substring check is sloppy
issues.detail: Substring match against a base URL will misclassify any future mirror or proxy whose hostname contains that string. Use startswith, or better, urlparse and compare host+path prefix. Small thing, but this is the kind of casual string match that bites three years later.

review.summary: The patch solves a real DNF5 bug with a reasonable approach: stop trusting upstream URLs, synthesize the coreos-pool path yourself. Good instinct. But the execution has two real defects: extract_arch_from_url silently returns None and the caller will happily build a URL with the string 'None' in it, and nevra[0] takes the first character of the filename rather than the package name — works by accident today, breaks tomorrow. The race condition with coreos-koji-tagger is honestly disclosed but not mitigated in the code. NEEDS-WORK: fail loudly on missing arch, parse the NEVRA properly, lift the constants, add a test.
